WHAT YOU WILL GET

Why Choose H.g generalbuildin

You are not really choosing a contractor. You are choosing whether the next six months in your own house are calm or miserable. Here is what you get with us:

Get My Estimate

You Always Know What Is Next

A written schedule, updated every week. You should never have to ask what is happening inside your own house.

The Number Does Not Move

Your estimate is line-item and fixed. Any change needs your approval in writing before it happens.

Licensed, Bonded And Insured

Every trade on your property is covered. If something goes wrong, it is not yours to pay for.

We Answer The Phone

Same person, same number, the whole job. Most calls come back the same day.

Permits Before Demo

We do not open a wall until the paperwork is approved. Slower on day one, far faster after.

We Come Back

If something is not right in the first year, we fix it. That is the whole warranty — there is no fine print.

Our Expertise

Why The Cheapest Bid Usually Costs The Most

The lowest quote is almost always the one missing something. Permits. Waterproofing. The wiring that has to come up to code the moment the wall is open. None of it disappears — it comes back as a change order after you have already committed. We price the whole job, including the parts nobody likes to bring up. It makes our number look higher on day one, and lower on the last day.

A few things a licensed general contractor carries for you that you would otherwise carry yourself:

Get My Estimate

Permits

We pull them and meet the inspectors. Unpermitted work is the thing that surfaces years later, when you go to sell.

Insurance

Every crew on site is covered. Without that, someone getting hurt on your property can become your liability.

Cost Estimates

A written line-item scope, so you can hold us against another bid line by line instead of guessing which one is honest.

Trade Connections

Electricians, plumbers and tile setters we have worked with for years. They show up for us because we keep them busy.

Shorter Timeline

Trades booked in the right order. Most delays are not slow work — they are one crew waiting on another.

General Contractor in Brentwood

H.g generalbuildin builds and remodels homes across Brentwood and the surrounding area. Kitchens, bathrooms, additions, whole-house remodels and ground-up builds. Every job starts the same way: we walk the space, put a line-item scope in writing, and give you a date.

You will work with one person the entire time. They pull the permits, book the trades in the right order, meet the inspectors, and tell you the moment something changes. That is the whole difference between a remodel you barely notice and one you are still telling people about two years later.

Get My Estimate

Commercial Build-Outs And Tenant Improvements

We also take on commercial work — offices, retail spaces and tenant improvements. The pressure there is different: every extra week is rent on a space you cannot open yet.

So we sequence the trades around your opening date and work outside business hours where the space is already occupied. You get the same written scope and the same single point of contact.

Show More

If you are comparing bids, ask each one who your day-to-day contact is and what happens when an inspection fails. The answers tell you more than the number does.

What To Ask Before You Sign With Any Contractor

Ask to see the licence and the certificate of insurance, and check the dates. Ask who is actually on site every day and whether they are employees or subs. Ask what happens if an inspection fails — a good answer is specific, not reassuring.

Ask how change orders work. If the answer is "we will let you know", that is how a bid grows by a third. It should be: nothing changes without your signature and a new number, in writing, first.

Show More

Ask for the last three jobs like yours and call one of them. Not the reference list — the last three. Anyone can produce three happy customers. Far fewer can produce their three most recent ones.

We are happy to answer all of that on the first visit, and we would rather you asked the same of everyone else you are considering.
